newsitem.title: UK: Japan's Eisai seeks 35 pct of sales abroad.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Eisai seeks 35 pct of sales abroad.

text.p: Japanese pharmaceutical group Eisai Co Ltd said on Thursday that it was aiming to achieve 35 percent of its sales outside Japan, compared with under 10 percent at present.

In an interview with Reuters, president and chief executive officer Haruo Naito said "We'd like to have something like 35 percent of sales from the U.S, Asia and Europe. Now we have less than 10 percent from outside, so it woud be a substantial increase."
Naito was speaking ahead of the company's expansion of its operations in Europe, which includes the establishment of subsidiaries in Britain, France and Germany.
Last year Eisai's sales totalled 273 billion yen, mostly in Japan. The company currently has no presence on the European market, apart from one product licensed to Germany's Boehringer Mannheim.

The group plans to launch Aricept for treatment of mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease in the UK in April, followed by a launch in Germany in the summer or autumn and France in the middle of 1998, Naito said.
"Through several products we will launch here in the EU we'd like to get $300 million of sales in five years," Naito added.

Naito said the next product to be launched in Europe would be anti-ulcer drug Pariet, which was filed with British regulators in January. Other drugs likely to be launched in Europe include a treatment for septic shock and a number of cancer products.
He said the the Japanese company expected to invest $30 million to $40 million over the next two to three years" in Europe as it established marketing and sales infrastructure.
Naito said it would also establish a European manufacturing base, although "not soon".
He declined to be drawn on whether Britain, which houses Eisai's only European research operation and its European headquarters, would be a possible manufacturing base.
"I know that the UK likes to invite a lot of investment from our industry here, so we would certainly like to think about it," Naito said.
